correctness.rationale: For any compactly supported invariant probability, second-coordinate invariance gives \(\mathbb E[Y]=b\mathbb E[X]\), while first-coordinate invariance gives \(1=a\mathbb E[|X|]+(1-b)\mathbb E[X]\). Decomposing \(X\) into positive and negative parts yields the exact weighted budget. The two barycenter-defect identities follow by elimination and \(A+B=2a\); the packaged symbolic checker reproduces those reductions. Endpoint equality forces one sign of \(X\) to vanish. With \(b>0\), the support then lies on one affine branch. Translating the corresponding fixed point produces an invertible real hyperbolic linear map; compact two-sided invariance leaves only the origin, proving Dirac rigidity. The proof uses no finite enumeration or asymptotic extrapolation.

value.rationale: The claim is a natural structural constraint on stationary statistics of a canonical piecewise-linear chaotic map. It is sharp because the endpoints are exactly the two fixed points, and its defect formulas quantify how far the barycenter lies from each endpoint by the opposite-sign first-moment visitation. This yields a rigorous obstruction to one-sided non-equilibrium compact recurrence and a parameter-explicit benchmark for numerical periodic or chaotic invariant measures. It is not merely a renamed fixed-point calculation: the statement applies uniformly to every compact invariant probability and includes exact rigidity at the boundary.
